claim.quote: This letter describes the observation of the light-by-light scattering process, gamma gamma -> gamma gamma, in Pb+Pb collisions at sqrt(s_NN) = 5.02 TeV.

significance.quote: The observed excess of events over the expected background has a significance of 8.2 standard deviations.

summary.plain: ATLAS watched two particles of light bounce off each other - a process so rare it needs the electromagnetic fields of whole lead nuclei grazing past one another to see it at all.
summary.technical: Ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions at 5.02 TeV per nucleon pair, 1.73 nb^-1 (Nov 2018): 59 gamma-gamma -> gamma-gamma candidates against a background of 12 +/- 3 events, 8.2 sigma significance, fiducial cross section 78 +/- 13 (stat.) +/- 7 (syst.) +/- 3 (lumi.) nb.

title: Observation of light-by-light scattering in ultraperipheral Pb+Pb collisions with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: Light-by-light scattering is forbidden in classical electrodynamics and occurs only through virtual charged-particle loops in QED; observing it directly tests the Standard Model in an extreme low-background regime and constrains new light, weakly-charged particles.
